Khichdi

Served at: Gita Jayanti (गीता जयंती)

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 30 min

Khichdi is a comforting and wholesome one-pot dish made with rice and lentils, often seasoned with mild spices. It is traditionally served during Gita Jayanti, a day celebrating the Bhagavad Gita, symbolizing simplicity and nourishment for both body and soul.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup basmati rice (200 g)
  • 1/2 cup yellow moong dal (split yellow gram) (100 g)
  • 4 cups water (960 ml)
  • 1 tablespoon ghee (clarified butter) (15 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon cumin seeds
  • 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
  • 1 teaspoon grated ginger
  • 1-2 green chilies, slit (optional)
  • Salt to taste
  • Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Method

  1. Rinse the rice and moong dal together under cold water until the water runs clear.
  2. In a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot, heat the ghee over medium heat.
  3. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
  4. Add grated ginger and green chilies, sauté for 1 minute.
  5. Add the rinsed rice and dal, turmeric powder, and salt; stir well to combine.
  6. Pour in the water and bring it to a boil.
  7. If using a pressure cooker, cover and cook for 3-4 whistles on medium heat. If using a pot, cover and simmer until rice and dal are soft and cooked through, about 25-30 minutes.
  8. Once cooked, gently fluff the khichdi with a spoon.
  9. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves before serving.

Tips

  • Adjust the consistency by adding more water for a softer, porridge-like khichdi.
  • Serve with a dollop of ghee on top for enhanced flavor and richness.
  • Pair khichdi with yogurt, pickle, or papad for a complete traditional meal.
